extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, editorial board members, reviewers, journal owners and publishers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for good publication practice covering study design, data analysis, authorship, conflicts of interest, peer review, redundant publication, plagiarism, duties of editors, media relations, advertising, and handling misconduct in biomedical/scientific journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research driven by protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory and clinical research should be driven by protocol; pilot studies should have a written rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols provide structure and justification for research; pilot studies require a written rationale to justify methods and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocols answer specific questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Research protocols should seek to answer specific questions, rather than just collect data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design studies to test hypotheses or answer predefined questions to avoid aimless data collection that may constitute poor practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreement on protocol among contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Protocols must be carefully agreed by all contributors and collaborators, including, if appropriate, the participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early, documented agreement reduces later disputes and helps clarify roles/responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final protocol retention
rubrics_metrics.description: The final protocol should form part of the research record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep protocol as a permanent part of study documentation for audit, replication, and ethical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early agreement on roles and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Early agreement on the precise roles of the contributors and collaborators, and on matters of authorship and publication, is advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document contributor roles and authorship criteria early to avoid disputes and ensure fair credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical planning and power calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Statistical issues should be considered early in study design, including power calculations, to ensure there are neither too few nor too many participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider sample size and analysis plans at design stage to produce reliable, ethical studies and avoid waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical approval for studies involving humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal and documented ethical approval from an appropriately constituted research ethics committee is required for all studies involving people, medical records, and anonymised human tissues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not proceed without documented approval; this applies to identifiable and anonymised human materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: High ethical standard for human tissue use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of human tissues in research should conform to the highest ethical standards, such as those recommended by the Nuffield Council on Bioethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow recognized national/international guidance when using human tissues; obtain appropriate approvals and consents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek fully informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully informed consent should always be sought; where not possible, an appropriately constituted research ethics committee should decide if this is acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document consent attempts; if consent cannot be obtained evaluate ethical acceptability via committee review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special guidance when participants cannot consent
rubrics_metrics.description: When participants are unable to give fully informed consent, research should follow international guidelines, such as those of CIOMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply internationally recognized safeguards and standards for research involving incapacitated participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal experiments compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal experiments require full compliance with local, national, ethical, and regulatory principles, and local licensing arrangements; international standards vary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow applicable local and national laws, licensing, and best-practice animal welfare standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal supervision, quality control, and record retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal supervision, usually the responsibility of the principal investigator, should be provided for all research projects and must include quality control and frequent review; long term retention (may be up to 15 years) of all records and primary outputs is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PI should oversee quality assurance and ensure secure long-term storage/retention of primary data and records for audits or investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full disclosure of data sources and preprocessing
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources and methods used to obtain and analyze data, including any electronic pre-processing, should be fully disclosed; detailed explanations should be provided for any exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparent reporting of data provenance and any preprocessing steps enables reproducibility and assessment of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and reference analysis methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of analysis must be explained in detail, and referenced, if they are not in common use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail so others can evaluate and reproduce analyses; cite specialized methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose post hoc subgroup analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: The post hoc analysis of subgroups is acceptable, as long as this is disclosed. Failure to disclose that the analysis was post hoc is unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label exploratory/post hoc findings clearly to avoid misleading claims of pre-specified hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss bias in Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion section of a paper should mention any issues of bias which have been considered, and explain how they have been dealt with in the design and interpretation of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should transparently discuss potential biases and limitations and how they impact interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship requires substantive intellectual contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The award of authorship should balance intellectual contributions to the conception, design, analysis and writing of the study against the collection of data and other routine work; if there is no task that can reasonably be attributed to a particular individual, then that individual should not be credited with authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorship should reflect meaningful scholarly contribution, not routine or administrative tasks alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide authorship, contributors, acknowledgements early
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid disputes over attribution of academic credit, it is helpful to decide early on in the planning of a research project who will be credited as authors, as contributors, and who will be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document early agreements and update them if roles change; communicate decisions to all participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors take public responsibility for content
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must take public responsibility for the content of their paper; where multidisciplinary contributions complicate this, disclose individual contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contributor statements to clarify responsibility for sections or aspects of the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult target journal’s advice to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful reading of the target journal’s 'Advice to Authors' is advised, in the light of current uncertainties about authorship definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific authorship and disclosure requirements of the target journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define conflicts of interest broadly
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest comprise those which may not be fully apparent and which may influence the judgement of authors, reviewers, and editors; they may be personal, commercial, political, academic or financial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider types of interests including employment, funding, stock ownership, payments, consultancies, and company support for staff when assessing COI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare relevant interests to editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Such interests, where relevant, must be declared to editors by researchers, authors, and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, disclose; disclosure enables editors and readers to assess possible biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors disclose their conflicts and sometimes withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should also disclose relevant conflicts of interest to their readers. If in doubt, disclose. Sometimes editors may need to withdraw from the review and selection process for the relevant submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be transparent and recuse themselves from handling submissions when conflicts could affect impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use author suggestions for reviewers with no obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestions from authors as to who might act as reviewers are often useful, but there should be no obligations on editors to use those suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may consider author-suggested reviewers but must retain independence in reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain reviewer confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The duty of confidentiality in the assessment of a manuscript must be maintained by expert reviewers, and this extends to reviewers’ colleagues who may be asked (with the editor’s permission) to give opinions on specific sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep manuscript content and review process confidential; obtain editor permission before consulting others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not retain or copy submitted manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitted manuscript should not be retained or copied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect the authors’ intellectual property; return or securely store any materials per journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of data by reviewers or editors without permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and editors should not make any use of the data, arguments, or interpretations, unless they have the authors’ permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exploiting privileged information from peer review for personal or professional advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers should provide timely, courteous, unbiased reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should provide speedy, accurate, courteous, unbiased and justifiable reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness, professionalism, and impartiality are expected in review reports; provide evidence-based critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report suspected misconduct to editor in confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers suspect misconduct, they should write in confidence to the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate suspicions privately with supporting evidence rather than raising allegations publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish accurate descriptions of peer review processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should publish accurate descriptions of their peer review, selection, and appeals processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency about peer review models and appeals improves trust and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide audits of acceptance rates and publication times
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals should also provide regular audits of their acceptance rates and publication times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic reporting of performance metrics helps authors judge journal practices and timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant publication definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Redundant publication occurs when two or more papers, without full cross reference, share the same hypothesis, data, discussion points, or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting overlapping manuscripts without transparent cross-referencing and disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior abstracts from meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous publications of an abstract during the proceedings of meetings does not preclude subsequent submission for publication, but full disclosure should be made at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose prior presentations or abstracts when submitting full manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-publication in another language allowed with disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-publication of a paper in another language is acceptable, provided that there is full and prominent disclosure of its original source at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear citation and disclosure of prior language-version publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose related papers at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of submission, authors should disclose details of related papers, even if in a different language, and similar papers in press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete transparency about related works helps editors to assess novelty and redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism prohibition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Plagiarism ranges from the unreferenced use of others’ published and unpublished ideas (including research grant applications) to submission under 'new' authorship of a complete paper; it may occur at any stage and applies to print and electronic versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that plagiarism includes reuse of ideas and text across stages and media; journals treat it seriously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose sources and seek permission for large reuse
rubrics_metrics.description: All sources should be disclosed, and if large amounts of other people’s written or illustrative material is to be used, permission must be sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite sources and obtain permissions where substantial quoted or illustrated material is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors are stewards of journals and must balance interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must consider and balance the interests of many constituents, including readers, authors, staff, owners, editorial board members, advertisers and the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions should weigh multiple stakeholders’ interests while maintaining integrity and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published studies need not be repeated routinely
rubrics_metrics.description: Published studies do not need to be repeated unless further confirmation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replication should be conducted when necessary to confirm findings; routine duplication is not always required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decisions based solely on scholarly merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors’ decisions to accept or reject a paper for publication should be based only on the paper’s importance, originality, and clarity, and the study’s relevance to the remit of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude non-scholarly influences (e.g., commercial pressures) from acceptance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give sympathetic hearing to studies challenging prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies that challenge previous work published in the journal should be given an especially sympathetic hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage critical discourse and fair consideration of studies that question established findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish negative results
rubrics_metrics.description: Studies reporting negative results should not be excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value negative and null results to reduce publication bias and provide a fuller scientific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review original studies before publication
rubrics_metrics.description: All original studies should be peer reviewed before publication, taking into full account possible bias due to related or conflicting interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure peer review is applied consistently and that reviewers are alerted to potential COI affecting impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat all submitted papers as confidential
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must treat all submitted papers as confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain confidentiality of submissions and reviewer identities as per journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct the record promptly when flaws are found
rubrics_metrics.description: When a published paper is subsequently found to contain major flaws, editors must accept responsibility for correcting the record prominently and promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue corrections, retractions, or notices as required and inform indexing services and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advise authors of journal media policies
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be helpful to authors to be advised of any media policies operated by the journal in which their work is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communicate media interaction rules and embargo policies to authors at submission and acceptance stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors give balanced account to the media
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors approached by the media should give as balanced an account of their work as possible, ensuring that they point out where evidence ends and speculation begins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overstatement; clearly distinguish evidence-based findings from hypotheses or speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous mass media and peer-reviewed publication advised
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous publication in the mass media and a peer reviewed journal is advised, as this usually means that enough evidence and data have been provided to satisfy informed and critical readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinated release can help ensure accuracy; follow journal embargo policies and provide appropriate supporting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help journalists but avoid supplying extra unpublished data
rubrics_metrics.description: Where simultaneous publication is not possible, authors should help journalists to produce accurate reports, but refrain from supplying additional data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear explanations without releasing unpublished or additional data that could mislead or preempt peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inform patients of results before mass media
rubrics_metrics.description: All efforts should be made to ensure that patients who have helped with the research should be informed of the results by the authors before the mass media, especially if there are clinical implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect participant confidentiality and prioritize communicating findings to participants prior to public release when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors should be advised if journalists will attend meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be advised by the organizers if journalists are to attend scientific meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authors know about media presence to prepare appropriate communications and consent for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of editorial and advertising administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions must not be influenced by advertising revenue or reprint potential: editorial and advertising administration must be clearly separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain structural and procedural separation to prevent commercial influence on content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse misleading advertisements and allow criticisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertisements that mislead must be refused, and editors must be willing to publish criticisms, according to the same criteria used for material in the rest of the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply consistent standards to advertising and editorial content; permit critical responses when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish reprints as they appear unless corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: Reprints should be published as they appear in the journal unless a correction is to be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter reprinted content except to append corrections; maintain integrity of the original publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct defined by intention to deceive
rubrics_metrics.description: The general principle confirming misconduct is intention to cause others to regard as true that which is not true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether actions were deliberate, reckless, or negligent when judging misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate intention as part of misconduct assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination of misconduct must focus not only on the act or omission, but also on the intention of the researcher, author, editor, reviewer or publisher involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate deliberate fraud from honest error or negligence when determining sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deception includes intention, reckless disregard, or negligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Deception may be by intention, by reckless disregard of possible consequences, or by negligence; best practice requires complete honesty and full disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider degrees of culpability and apply proportional responses; encourage transparency and reporting of honest errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes of practice raise awareness but are not exhaustive
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes of practice may raise awareness, but can never be exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use guidelines as frameworks; apply judgement to novel situations and seek advice where uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors must pursue suspected misconduct, not simply reject papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should not simply reject papers that raise questions of misconduct; they are ethically obliged to pursue the case, though investigating and responding can be difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open inquiries appropriately, seek expert advice, and follow fair procedures rather than dismissing suspect submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: COPE provides anonymised advice; editor decides action
rubrics_metrics.description: COPE is willing to advise but for legal reasons can only advise on anonymised cases; it is for the editor to decide what action to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors may consult COPE for guidance but retain responsibility for decisions and must consider legal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors often lack legal means to investigate serious misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must take allegations seriously but often do not have the legal legitimacy or means to conduct investigations into serious cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When investigations require legal authority, editors should refer cases to employers or appropriate bodies rather than attempting full investigations themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide when to alert employers
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor must decide when to alert the employers of the accused author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alert employers when evidence suggests serious misconduct or when employer investigation is the proper channel; balance confidentiality and duty to protect the scientific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assemble full case if employers have investigative processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Some evidence is required, but if employers have a process for investigating accusations, editors do not need to assemble a complete case and may ethically avoid doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient information to trigger employer investigation, but avoid investigative steps that might inappropriately publicize allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer convincing evidence of serious misconduct to employers immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: If presented with convincing evidence, perhaps by reviewers, of serious misconduct, editors should immediately pass this on to the employers and notify the author(s) that they are doing so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share evidence confidentially with appropriate institutional authorities and inform implicated authors of the referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek expert advice when evidence is not convincing
rubrics_metrics.description: If accusations of serious misconduct are not accompanied by convincing evidence, editors should confidentially seek expert advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent experts to assess allegations before escalating or making public accusations.

rubrics_metrics.name: If experts find serious concerns, notify employers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the experts raise serious questions about the research, then editors should notify the employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalate to institutional bodies when impartial review indicates substantive concerns requiring formal investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If no evidence of misconduct is found, proceed normally
rubrics_metrics.description: If the experts find no evidence of misconduct, the editorial processes should proceed in the normal way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unduly penalizing authors when independent review clears concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer doctors to professional regulators if no employer exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If presented with convincing evidence of serious misconduct where there is no employer to whom this can be referred, and the author(s) are registered doctors, cases can be referred to the General Medical Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use professional regulators as appropriate when institutional referral is unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish something if no investigating body exists (with legal advice)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no organization with the legitimacy and means to conduct an investigation, the editor may decide that the case is sufficiently important to warrant publishing something in the journal; legal advice will then be essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider public disclosure only after legal consultation and careful weighing of risks to individuals and the scientific record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give authors opportunity to respond to accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be given the opportunity to respond to accusations of serious misconduct (and to any charge of minor misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow fair procedures by allowing authors to present explanations before final decisions or sanctions are imposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle less serious misconduct possibly without employers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors may judge that it is not necessary to involve employers in less serious cases of misconduct (e.g., redundant publication, deception over authorship, failure to declare conflict of interest); sometimes appoint an independent expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proportionate responses for minor breaches; consider independent review where evidence is ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remember serious implications of minor accusations
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should remember that accusations of even minor misconduct may have serious implications for the author(s), and it may then be necessary to ask the employers to investigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh reputational consequences and consider institutional involvement when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions can be applied singly or combined
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions may be applied separately or combined and are ranked in approximate order of severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select appropriate sanctions proportionate to the severity and intent of the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational letter as sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of explanation (and education) to the authors, where there appears to be a genuine misunderstanding of principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use educational responses for inadvertent or minor breaches to correct behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of reprimand and warning
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of reprimand and warning as to future conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue formal warnings for more serious or repeated breaches to document concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal letter to head of institution or funding body
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal letter to the relevant head of institution or funding body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform institutional leadership when behaviour warrants formal institutional awareness or action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of notice of redundant publication or plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of a notice of redundant publication or plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly note the problem in the journal to correct the record and alert readers and indexing services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial describing the misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: An editorial giving full details of the misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider publishing an editorial when the matter has broad implications for the field or journal policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal of future submissions for a stated period
rubrics_metrics.description: Refusal to accept future submissions from the individual, unit, or institution responsible for the misconduct, for a stated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use temporary bans as a deterrent and protective measure for journal integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal withdrawal or retraction and notify indexing services
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal withdrawal or retraction of the paper from the scientific literature, informing other editors and the indexing authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retract flawed or fraudulent work prominently and inform databases and other journals to maintain the integrity of the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report to professional/regulatory bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting the case to the General Medical Council, or other such authority or organization which can investigate and act with due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer serious or professional misconduct to appropriate regulatory bodies for investigation and sanction where appropriate.
